summary: Per-page UI/UX review of every captured Ryan Realty page across 7 dimensions, then adversarial verification of P0/P1 findings. Complements the earlier cross-cutting run.

findings.title: Featured-homes rail on a $550K listing shows only $4M–$12M luxury estates
findings.evidence: listing-detail-desktop-11/12/13.png: the bottom 'Featured Homes' rail leads with $11,900,000, $8,750,000, $7,900,000, $5,995,000 and $4,995,000 estates while this home is $550,000. The eyebrow reads 'Bend Park · For sale' (listing-detail-desktop-10.png) but the tiles are Tetherow / Broken Top / Grandridge, not Bend Park. lib/kb/fetch-nearby-tiles.ts pulls sort:'price-desc' and, because Bend Park has <4 actives, widens to city-wide Bend still price-desc — so a mid-market buyer's only onward-navigation rail is the most expensive homes in the county. Same on mobile (listing-detail-mobile-15.png).
findings.fix: Re-rank the nearby-tiles rail by price proximity to this listing's list price (nearest first), or constrain to a price band (e.g. ±40%), instead of price-desc. Keep the widen-on-thin-scope fallback but re-sort after widening so a $550K buyer sees homes they'd actually consider.
findings._verify_note: Confirmed real, but P1 overstates it — downgrade to P2. Verified against screenshots: subject listing is 225 Vine Lane, $550K, 2BD/1BA/748sqft (listing-detail-desktop-01.png). The bottom 'Featured Homes' rail shows exclusively $4M–$12M estates — all twelve tiles across desktop-11/12/13 are $11.9M, $8.75M, $7.9M, $5.995M, $4.995M, $4.995M, $4.95M, $4M, $4M, $5.95M, $4.987M, $6.999M (8×–22× the subject). Eyebrow reads 'Bend Park · For sale' (desktop-10) but tiles are Tetherow / Broken Top / Grandridge / Enchantment / Lisle Acres, not Bend Park. Code confirms: lib/kb/fetch-nearby-tiles.ts sorts price-desc (lines 21,25) and widens neighborhood→city on thin scope, still price-desc — its own docstring calls it a 'Similar homes' rail, so this is a bug not an intended luxury showcase. Fix (re-rank by price proximity / ±band, re-sort after widening) is sound. Downgraded because: it's a below-the-fold secondary re-engagement rail, not the primary conversion path; the 'Schedule a Tour' CTA is unaffected; the rail still renders valid clickable homes plus a 'BROWSE HOMES' escape hatch. Nothing broken or blocked — a relevance degradation, which is P2, not a P1-class conversion blocker. Note the related widen-fallback code was itself logged 'design-audit P2'.

findings.title: Hero of an $11.9M listing displays a 'connection is not secure' block page instead of the property
findings.evidence: listing-luxury-desktop-01.png: the full-bleed hero shows large centered white text 'We couldn't verify the security of your connection. Access to this content has been restricted. Contact your internet service provider for help.' with the price band and an UNMUTE button beneath it. The hero video path in components/site/listing-detail/ListingHero.tsx (VideoLayer, iframe/video-tag embed) renders the embed full-bleed with no onError/health fallback, so a failed or filtered third-party video/tour URL surfaces its own error document as the single most prominent visual on the page.
findings.fix: In ListingHero's VideoLayer, add an onError (and load-timeout) handler on the iframe/video element that falls back to photos[0] full-bleed; never let an unreachable or non-video embed render as the hero. Health-check the embed URL server-side and only choose the video path when it resolves to real media.
findings._verify_note: Screenshot confirms the claim exactly: the $11.9M listing (65255 Swalley Road) hero renders a full-bleed third-party block page — 'We couldn't verify the security of your connection. Access to this content has been restricted. Contact your internet service provider for help.' — with the price band ($11.9M · 3 BD · 3 BA · 2,268 SQFT) and UNMUTE button overlaid, and the photo strip below. Root cause verified in components/site/listing-detail/ListingHero.tsx: VideoLayer's iframe path has no onError/load-timeout/health fallback, and posterUrl (photos[0]) is only used by the <video> path, so a failed/filtered iframe embed surfaces the remote host's own error document as the hero. The sibling ListingVideoEmbed.tsx already guards a hostile-embed case (Zillow/PerimeterX → link card), proving the class is known but ungated here. Caveat for the reader: the block-page wording points to a network-level filter on the capture machine as the immediate trigger, so not all production visitors would hit this exact page — but the code defect (zero error resilience on a full-bleed hero embed) is real, and any user on a filtered network sees an alarming security-error message as the entire first impression of the flagship listing. Keeping P0: catastrophic, trust-damaging failure mode on the highest-value listing's hero, cheap fix (onError → photos[0] fallback and/or server-side embed health check).

findings.title: Rental Analysis frames the trophy estate as a catastrophic rental with an obviously-wrong auto-rent
findings.evidence: listing-luxury-desktop-08.png and -09.png: for an $11.9M, 118-acre canyon estate the investor tool auto-fills Monthly rent $2,336 ('HUD Fair Market Rent (FY2025), Deschutes County, 3BR') and headlines Cash flow -$63,117/mo, Cap rate 0.0%, Cash on cash -31.8%, with prose 'this property runs $63,117 per month negative.' A $2,336 rent is self-evidently wrong for this property class, and the giant negative figures both undercut the luxury framing and dent the site's data credibility on the exact tier where a buyer scrutinizes numbers.
findings.fix: Gate the auto-seeded HUD FMR rent and/or the whole Rental Analysis above a price/property threshold (e.g. suppress or collapse behind an opt-in for luxury/estate listings), and don't render headline cash-flow numbers off a rent the module itself can't reasonably estimate. Target components/listing/InvestmentAnalysis.tsx.
findings._verify_note: Confirmed as real via listing-luxury-desktop-08/09.png: for the $11.9M / 118-acre estate the Rental Analysis auto-fills Monthly rent $2,336 labeled "HUD Fair Market Rent (FY2025), Deschutes County, 3BR", producing CASH FLOW -$63,117/mo, CAP RATE 0.0%, CASH ON CASH -31.8%, and prose "this property runs $63,117 per month negative." A HUD apartment FMR against an eight-figure estate is self-evidently wrong and dents data credibility on the tier where buyers scrutinize numbers most. Target component (components/listing/InvestmentAnalysis.tsx) and fix (gate HUD auto-seed / collapse module above a price threshold; don't headline cash-flow off an unreliable rent) are appropriate. Downgraded to P2 because: the module is well below the fold, every figure is explicitly disclaimered ("Every number is an estimate you can adjust", "Edit to your own number", full "not investment advice" block), the rent is user-editable, and a $11.9M canyon estate is virtually never evaluated as a rental so the conversion-loss surface is thin. The 0.0% cap rate is honest rounding of NOI $2,628/yr ÷ $11.9M (~0.02%), a downstream effect of the one bad rent seed, not a separate bug. Real credibility/polish issue, not a P1 conversion blocker.

findings.title: Track-record proof grid shows flat navy cards with no photo
findings.evidence: In team-member-desktop-04.png the '$661,000 · 20473 Jacklight' tile is a solid navy rectangle with only a price/address and no photo; team-member-desktop-05.png shows the same for '$1,191,000 · 1974 Newport Hills' and '$650,000 · 3480 45th'. Three of nine tiles in the 'Featured Homes / Track record' grid render as empty navy blocks. KbFeatured.client.tsx lines 86-92 fall back to `<div style={{background:'var(--navy)'}}>` whenever `it.img` is empty (missing MLS PhotoURL). This is the exact section meant to prove Matt's marketing quality, and the reviews directly below it (team-member-desktop-06.png) literally praise 'His presentation and marketing were professional and thorough' — empty tiles read as broken images and contradict that claim.
findings.fix: Filter photoless tiles out before the 3/6/9 row cap in page.tsx (brokerSaleItems.slice) so only tiles with a real PhotoURL fill the grid (6 good tiles beat 9 with 3 voids). If a branded state is preferred, replace the flat navy void with a Ryan Realty monogram + 'SOLD $X' stamp placeholder rather than an empty rectangle.
findings._verify_note: Verified in team-member-desktop-04.png: the "$661,000 / 20473 Jacklight" tile (bottom-left of the Featured Homes / Track record grid) is a uniform flat navy rectangle with only price + address + beds/baths/sqft and no photo. It is NOT a dark photo — the other four tiles ($3,025,000 School House, $755,000 Mayfield, $355,000 703 7th, $1,030,000 Old Bend Redmond Hwy) all show detailed house photography with clear tonal variation, while this tile has zero photographic content, gradient, or texture. It is the empty-image navy fallback. So 1 of 5 tiles in this image is a photoless void (the finding's "3 of 9" total also references image 05, which I did not open, but the defect class is confirmed). Kept at P1: this is the proof-of-marketing-quality section sitting directly above reviews praising Matt's presentation/marketing, and the void repeats across tiles, so a photoless card in the very grid meant to showcase listing photography is a real, non-trivial trust hit. Only mitigant is that the card degrades into a legible on-brand navy card rather than a broken-image icon — enough to keep it P1 rather than escalate, not enough to downgrade. Proposed fix (filter photoless tiles before the row cap, or substitute a branded SOLD stamp placeholder) is sound.

findings.title: "WATCH BEND" area-guide video renders as a raw browser player floating in a large empty navy void
findings.evidence: In city-bend-desktop-14.png the video is a small landscape poster centered in a tall empty navy band, with a default light-grey HTML5 media control (play, 0:00/0:30, volume, three-dot menu) sitting beneath it. In city-bend-mobile-15.png the video area is an entirely blank navy box (no visible poster) with only the same grey stock control pill. Source confirms KbAreaGuideVideo (components/site/kb/KbAreaGuideVideo.tsx) uses a native <video controls> element and its wide/aspect-ratio sizing (width:100% + maxHeight:70vh + aspectRatio 16/9) is producing a too-small poster on desktop and a poster-less navy block on mobile. On an otherwise premium editorial page this one section reads as unfinished/broken and dents trust.
findings.fix: In KbAreaGuideVideo, wrap the native player in branded chrome (a poster with object-fit:cover filling the framed 16/9 or 9/16 box and a design-system play-button overlay that swaps to the real player on click) so no default grey control bar shows at rest, and correct the sizing so the poster fills the framed area instead of leaving 50%+ empty navy. Verify the correct `wide` flag is passed for Bend so the landscape cut isn't being sized as portrait.
findings._verify_note: Verified against both screenshots. Desktop (14): small Mt. Bachelor landscape poster centered in a tall navy band with a default light-grey HTML5 media control pill (play, 0:00/0:30, volume, three-dot menu) floating beneath it, surrounded by large empty navy space. Mobile (15): the video region is an entirely blank navy box with no visible poster, only the same grey stock control pill. This is a raw native <video controls> element with no branded chrome, a clear design-system inconsistency (CLAUDE.md bans raw HTML controls) that reads as unfinished on an otherwise premium navy editorial page. Real at P1. Minor caveat: the fix's suggestion to check the `wide` flag is off for desktop — the desktop cut already renders correctly as landscape; the actual defects are the missing branded chrome and the sizing leaving 50%+ empty navy (worst on mobile, where the poster is absent entirely).

findings.title: Featured section degrades into a long run of full-screen zero-inventory cards
findings.evidence: The 'Resort & master-planned' rows render in curated registry order, NOT by inventory (app/communities/page.tsx lines 279-390; activeCount defaults to 0 at line 159). Strong active communities lead (Tetherow 25, Eagle Crest 40, Sunriver 60), but the entire back half collapses into '0 ACTIVE / MEDIAN LIST —' full-viewport cards: Widgi Creek, Vandevert Ranch, Three Rivers, then Inn of the 7th Mountain, Rivers Edge, Mountain High, Crooked River Ranch (communities-desktop-08 through -13; mobile-15). A shopper scanning this discovery hub for homes scrolls ~7 screen-height cards with nothing browsable and an empty stat band, on a page whose hero sells '641 homes for sale / live inventory from the regional MLS.'
findings.fix: Sort the `resorts` array by activeCount desc before render (stable within curated order), or partition the zero-active communities into a compact list/grid below the editorial rows instead of one full-viewport card each. Lead the section with browsable inventory.
findings._verify_note: Real and correctly diagnosed. Code confirms resorts render in curated registry order (not inventory-sorted; app/communities/page.tsx:124-163, render 279-390) with activeCount defaulting to 0 (line 159). Screenshots confirm strong rows lead (Pronghorn 15, Caldera Springs 32, Brasada 35) and the tail is dominated by full-width '0 Active / — Median list' editorial rows: Widgi Creek, Vandevert Ranch, Three Rivers, Inn of the 7th Mountain, Rivers Edge, Mountain High, Crooked River Ranch (7 of 8 tail rows zero), several with generic filler photos (Mountain High shows an alpine range labeled 'Area view · Bend'). Downgraded from P1 to P2 because: (1) the 'entire back half collapses' framing is overstated — Mt Bachelor Village (4 active / $509,000) interrupts the run mid-tail; (2) every zero row still carries working guide + 'Homes for sale in [City]' links, so inventory is reachable, this is not a dead end; (3) the '0 Active' display is a deliberate, documented honest-ledger design decision, not a defect; (4) the hero's 641-homes aggregate is accurate and a full A-to-Z index follows. Net effect is scroll fatigue and a weak impression of resort-inventory depth on the most prominent section — moderate friction, not a conversion-blocking flow break. Proposed fix (sort resorts by activeCount desc, or partition zero-active into a compact grid below the editorial rows) is valid.

findings.title: "Live · Tetherow · Latest market activity" shows non-Tetherow (Bend-wide) listings
findings.evidence: community-tetherow-desktop-14.png: the section eyebrow reads "Live · Tetherow" under the heading "Latest Market Activity," but the first card is "3782 Suchy Street — BEND · PETROSA — $749,000," a home in a different community entirely. Source confirms the mismatch: app/communities/[slug]/page.tsx line 311 feeds the feed with getActivityFeedWithFallbackMulti({ cities: [cityName], limit: 8 }) (city-scoped = all of Bend) while line 874 labels it eyebrow={`Live · ${community.name}`}. On a page whose hero promise is "the live market behind every one," a $749K Petrosa card under a Tetherow ($2.25M) label reads as wrong data and quietly erodes trust in every other live figure on the page.
findings.fix: Scope the activity query to the community (filter to Tetherow subdivision/alias listings) so the cards match the label; if Tetherow volume is too thin, relabel the eyebrow to "Bend · Latest market activity" and drop the community name so the section doesn't promise Tetherow-specific activity it isn't showing.
findings._verify_note: Both visual and source claims verified. Screenshot (community-tetherow-desktop-14.png) shows eyebrow "Live · Tetherow" over "LATEST MARKET ACTIVITY" / "LIVE · MLS · 8 UPDATES", with first card "3782 Suchy Street — BEND · PETROSA — $749,000 (NEW, MAY 1)" and second "18880 Baker Road — $4,050,000". Petrosa (NE Bend neighborhood) and Baker Road are not Tetherow (SW Bend golf-resort, $2M+ tier). The bottom-left "N" is the Next.js dev indicator and was ignored. Source confirms the mechanism precisely: app/communities/[slug]/page.tsx:311 feeds the section via getActivityFeedWithFallbackMulti({ cities: [cityName], limit: 8 }) — city-scoped (Bend), not community-scoped — while lines 872-874 hard-label the eyebrow `Live · ${community.name}`. This is a real, systemic label-vs-content contradiction on every community page: the section names the community but shows city-wide listings. Given the page's community-specific market promise and CLAUDE.md §0 data-accuracy mandate, P1 (trust) is the correct severity. Suggested fix from the finding is sound: scope the feed to the community subdivision/alias, or relabel the eyebrow to "Bend · Latest market activity" if community volume is too thin.

findings.title: Nearly every post card shows the identical Old Mill District drone photo
findings.evidence: blog-desktop-02/03/04/05 and blog-mobile-04: the featured 'Bend July 2026' card plus Central Oregon, Redmond, Sisters, Sunriver, La Pine, Price-per-sqft and Bend-June market-report cards all render the exact same three-smokestack Old Mill District aerial. Source confirms cards render per-post `post.hero_image_url` (app/blog/page.tsx line 280) and the featured `featured.hero_image_url` (line 223), so the authoring layer defaulted ~8 posts to one image. A blog whose job is to prove local expertise reads as auto-generated/templated, and using Bend's Old Mill for a 'Sisters' or 'Sunriver' report is subtly misleading.
findings.fix: Assign a distinct, town-specific hero image per post at authoring time (each market-report producer should pull imagery for its actual town, not the shared CONTENT_HERO_IMAGES.reports default). At minimum, rotate a small set of Central Oregon photos so no two adjacent cards match.
findings._verify_note: Verified against blog-desktop-02/03/04. Seven post cards render the byte-identical ground-level Old Mill District photo (three smokestacks, pond reflection, spring foliage): featured 'Bend July 2026' + Central Oregon + Redmond + Sisters + Sunriver + La Pine + a second Bend market-report card, several adjacent in the grid. Using Bend's Old Mill for Sisters, Sunriver, Redmond, and La Pine reports is geographically misleading on a blog badged 'Central Oregon · Guides and Insights' that exists to prove local expertise. Two minor write-up errors, neither material: 'nearly every' overstates it (7 of ~12 visible cards repeat; the rest use 3+ distinct photos), and the Price-per-sqft card actually uses a distinct green Deschutes aerial, not the shared image. Core claim, root cause (per-post hero_image_url defaulting), and fix are sound. Confirmed at P1.

findings.title: Hero eyebrow + breadcrumb collide with the H1 and sit on an unscrimmed bright photo
findings.evidence: buy-desktop-01.png: the top of the H1 'BUY A HOME IN' crosses directly through the eyebrow line '• CENTRAL OREGON · BUYERS' and the 'HOME / BUY' breadcrumb, which are also gray text placed over the bright, unshaded upper half of the aerial photo (the navy scrim only covers the lower portion). The stacked labels read as struck-through and half-illegible. The page source confirms this is a rendered collision, not a screenshot artifact: KbBreadcrumb (line 192, overlay) + .hero-tag eyebrow (line 213) sit at the top while the compact desktop hero (inline style line 194, min-height clamp 440-620px, height:auto) lets the tall two-line Amboqia H1 (line 216) crowd upward into them. A comment at lines 199-201 already notes the same overflow class of bug for mobile.
findings.fix: Add top clearance so the H1 never overlaps the eyebrow/breadcrumb (increase hero top padding or the min-height clamp, and/or add explicit margin above the H1), and extend the navy overlay/gradient scrim to the very top of the hero so the breadcrumb and eyebrow have reliable contrast against the sky. Verify at 1280 and 1440 widths.
findings._verify_note: Zoomed into the top-left hero band (crops at 2.1x). The finding overstates the defect. FALSE claims: (a) the H1 does NOT cross through the 'HOME / BUY' breadcrumb — the breadcrumb is at the very top with clear separation from the caps; (b) the labels are WHITE, not gray; (c) they are not 'struck-through and half-illegible' — the eyebrow 'CENTRAL OREGON · BUYERS' remains on its own distinct line above the H1 caps. What is actually true: the oversized two-line H1 'BUY A HOME IN' rises up so its top serifs sit tight against the underside of the eyebrow (cramped spacing, near-touching but not overprinting), and the top labels sit on a brighter/busier, lightly-scrimmed portion of the aerial photo which slightly lowers contrast on the trailing word 'BUYERS'. That is a minor polish/tightness nit in the hero, not a hard collision that ruins the first impression. The suggested fix (add top clearance above the H1, extend the scrim upward) is reasonable, but the P1 severity is not warranted given the text remains legible and there is no true overlap. Downgrading to P3.

findings.title: Page promises 214 luxury homes, shows 12, and the only "see more" link dumps the shopper into the entire unfiltered Bend market
findings.evidence: Hero states "214 homes above $1.5 million are active in Bend right now" (desktop-01), but only 12 cards render and the sole continuation is the text link "SEE ALL ACTIVE BEND HOMES" (desktop-03). Source app/luxury-homes-bend/page.tsx line 145 points that link at /homes-for-sale/bend — the full unfiltered market (all price points, median ~$800k), dropping the $1.5M+ luxury filter entirely. A luxury buyer who just scrolled $4M-$12M homes has no path to browse homes 13-214 as a luxury set; they are sent to the whole market. The link is also under-styled as a plain small-caps text link, not a button, so it is easy to miss.
findings.fix: Point the continuation at a luxury-scoped results URL (e.g. /homes-for-sale/bend?minPrice=1500000 or a dedicated luxury filter) so it delivers the remaining ~200 luxury listings the headline promises, and relabel it "See all luxury homes in Bend." Promote it from a bare text link to a <Button> so the primary browse action reads as actionable.
findings._verify_note: Every factual claim verified against source + screenshots. Hero "214 homes above $1.5 million" is live from getListingTilesCount (page.tsx:100-101), page.tsx:54 caps the grid at limit:12, and page.tsx:145 links the sole continuation at /homes-for-sale/bend with no minPrice — dropping the $1.5M+ luxury filter. desktop-03 confirms the last cards ($4M) are followed by a bare small-caps "SEE ALL ACTIVE BEND HOMES" text link, not a button. The promise/delivery mismatch and unscoped continuation are real. Downgrading from P1 to P2: the link is functional (not broken) and /homes-for-sale/bend has its own price filters the shopper can reapply; the page carries other conversion paths (Set up an alert CTA at :116, five community chips at :162-170, 12 listing-detail links); and this is a self-described page-2 SEO landing page, not a core flow. Genuine improvement (scope the URL to luxury, relabel "See all luxury homes in Bend," promote to a Button) but moderate friction, not a severe broken flow.

findings.title: Empty 'Sponsored' ad card breaks the resource hub and can leak to competitors
findings.evidence: resources-desktop-02.png (and the zoomed crop) shows a large empty white card labeled 'SPONSORED' with zero content sitting between the resource grid and the valuation CTA, roughly 250px of dead space that reads as broken/unfinished. Source app/resources/page.tsx renders a live Google AdSense unit: `<AdUnit slot="1001003003" format="horizontal" />`. When ad inventory doesn't fill (common for a small local site) the visitor sees this empty box; when it does fill, AdSense can serve a rival brokerage's ad in the middle of Ryan Realty's own resource page.
findings.fix: Remove the AdUnit section from /resources entirely. A third-party ad slot on a first-party conversion hub either shows an empty box or sends the visitor to a competitor. Replace the space with a branded internal promo (market report or valuation) or simply delete the section so the grid flows straight into the valuation CTA.
findings._verify_note: Confirmed in both screenshot and source. resources-desktop-02.png shows a large blank white card labeled "SPONSORED" between the resource grid and the "Curious what your home is worth?" valuation CTA — ~240px of dead space that reads as broken/unfinished (distinct from the bottom-left Next.js "N" dev indicator). Source verified: app/resources/page.tsx:183 renders <AdUnit slot="1001003003" format="horizontal" /> inside <section id="resource-ad" aria-label="Sponsored">. components/AdUnit.tsx:50-64 always renders the Card + "Sponsored" label wrapper (minHeight 120) even when the AdSense <ins> gets no fill, which is exactly the empty box captured. The competitor-leak angle is also legitimate: default AdSense on a real-estate page can serve rival brokerage/portal ads on a first-party lead-conversion hub. Nuance (does not change verdict): the box only renders when marketing consent is granted AND the slot fails to fill (canRender gate at line 48), but the screenshot proves that real state occurs. P1 holds — prominent visual defect plus real trust/strategic risk on a conversion page; not P0 (page still works), not P2 polish. Fix as stated: remove the AdUnit section or replace with a branded internal promo so the grid flows into the valuation CTA.

findings.title: Empty open-house feed renders as a silent void — the page promises open houses and delivers only a seller pitch
findings.evidence: The hero (open-houses-desktop-01.png) reads 'OPEN HOUSES IN CENTRAL OREGON', but the very next section (open-houses-desktop-02.png) is 'WHAT'S YOUR HOME WORTH?' followed by the 'LET'S TALK' contact block and footer (open-houses-desktop-03/04.png). There is not one open house, date, photo, or address on the entire page — no heading, no 'none scheduled', nothing. Source proves it: components/site/kb/KbOpenHouses.client.tsx:127 `if (items.length === 0) return null` (the whole section disappears), and app/open-houses/page.tsx:211 gates the map on `mapFeatures.length > 0`. Because page.tsx:114 wraps the query in `withTimeoutFallback(..., [], 4000)`, a slow/failed MLS pull ALSO yields this same blank page, indistinguishable from a genuinely empty week. A visitor arriving from Google (meta promises 'Live list from the regional MLS with times, photos, and prices') cannot tell if there are no open houses, the page broke, or they're on the wrong page — and is handed a home-valuation form instead.
findings.fix: Replace `return null` with an explicit empty state that keeps the section shell: the 'Open houses' heading plus a plain line like 'No open houses scheduled in Central Oregon right now' and a clear next action ('Get notified when new ones post' / 'Browse all homes for sale'). Render this same state when the timeout fallback `[]` fires so a data stall never silently erases the core surface. Never let the page skip from the open-houses hero directly to the seller section.
findings._verify_note: Real and confirmed by both screenshots and source. Screenshot 01 (open-houses hero) flows directly into screenshot 02 ("What's your home worth?" seller section) with zero open-house content between — no list, date, photo, or address. Code confirms every mechanism: KbOpenHouses.client.tsx:127 `if (items.length === 0) return null` unmounts the whole section; page.tsx:211 gates the map on `mapFeatures.length > 0`; page.tsx:114 wraps the query in `withTimeoutFallback(..., [], 4000)`, so a slow/failed MLS pull produces the identical blank collapse (real reliability concern). The hero count is also suppressed on empty (`openHouseCount || null` → null), so nothing signals "no open houses." Downgraded to P1 because the finding's framing overstates: the page is not broken/unusable — nav, hero, seller, and footer all render, and the hero itself carries a "BROWSE →" CTA (visible in screenshot 01), so the visitor does have a next action, contradicting "handed a home-valuation form instead." This is a missing-empty-state / silent-collapse defect on the core section that surfaces only when the feed is empty (dead week or data stall) — serious UX and reliability gap, but not a page outage or data-accuracy/compliance breach. The proposed fix (explicit empty-state shell rendered on both the genuinely-empty and timeout `[]` paths) is correct.

A first-time visitor scrolling into the listings showcase sees a broken-looking void as the highest-value featured home.
