findings.fix: Apply a Google Maps styled-JSON to the KbListingMap that dims/suppresses administrative + locality labels beneath the cluster layer, and give the top-left stat overlay a solid navy pill background (not transparent-over-map) so 'LIVE · 1,871 ACTIVE LISTINGS' never sits on a base-map label.

findings.title: Featured card shows a truncated place name 'Fairway Point Villag' (missing final letter, no ellipsis)
findings.evidence: home-desktop-06.png and home-mobile-06.png both show the $945,000 / 17777 Topflite Lane card labeled 'Fairway Point Villag · Sunriver' — the word 'Village' is cut to 'Villag' with no ellipsis, so it reads as a typo rather than an intentional truncation. Small but it undercuts the 'real numbers, direct from the brokers' precision the hero promises.
findings.fix: Trace the featured card's subdivision/location string in the KbFeatured tile mapping; allow the full 'Fairway Point Village' to render (widen the field or wrap), and if a hard clip is required use a real ellipsis. Confirm the source value isn't itself a truncated MLS SubdivisionName.

findings.title: Map view is unreachable on mobile — no List/Map switcher renders
findings.evidence: On desktop the map is a co-equal, ~65%-of-screen discovery mode with a prominent Split/List/Map toggle (search-desktop-01.png). On mobile the controls row [mic][Newest][Save this search] and the filter chips lead straight into '848 homes in this area' and the card list with NO List/Map switcher and no floating 'Map' button anywhere across search-mobile-01/02/03/04.png. The count text is emitted by MapSearchView, whose mobile List/Map ToggleGroup (components/search/MapSearchView.tsx:565-580, the ONLY mobile map switcher on this page) is coded but not appearing — so mobile visitors, the majority of real-estate traffic, cannot open the map at all.
findings.fix: Debug why MapSearchView's mobile ToggleGroup (MapSearchView.tsx:565) does not render on the phone viewport and restore it; as a belt-and-suspenders, add a persistent floating 'Map' pill bottom-center in list mode (Zillow/Redfin pattern) so the map is always one tap away.

findings.title: Map markers overlap heavily in central Bend, making pins unreadable/unclickable
findings.evidence: In search-desktop-01.png the dense core of Bend is a pile-up of individual price pins and numbered cluster bubbles stacking on top of each other ($379k, $830k, $699k, $1.0M and cluster circles literally overlapping), so several prices are partly occluded and adjacent pins are hard to target. On a map-first search surface this defeats the purpose of the map.
findings.fix: Raise the clustering zoom threshold so overlapping individual pins collapse into cluster bubbles at this zoom, and/or add collision de-overlap (or spiderfy on click) in SearchMapClustered so no two markers occlude each other.

findings.title: Unlabeled voice-search mic button reads as ambiguous, and is over-weighted on mobile
findings.evidence: A bare microphone icon sits beside the search field on desktop (search-desktop-01.png) and, on mobile, becomes a large square button carrying equal visual weight to 'Sort' and 'Save this search' (search-mobile-01.png). A normal user cannot tell what it does, and it competes with the actual search input right next to it.
findings.fix: Add an accessible label + hover/long-press tooltip ('Search by voice'), and on mobile reduce its prominence (fold it into the search field as a trailing icon rather than a standalone control equal to Sort/Save).

findings.title: 'Remove boundary' map control uses insider jargon
findings.evidence: The top-right map control reads 'Remove boundary' (search-desktop-01.png). 'Boundary' is internal terminology — a first-time visitor won't know it refers to the drawn/city search-area outline or what removing it does to their results.
findings.fix: Rename to plain language such as 'Clear map area' or 'Search beyond this area', and add a one-line tooltip explaining it widens the search past the current outline.

findings.title: Split-view card rail is cramped — location line truncates mid-word
findings.evidence: In split view the map takes ~65% of the width and the homes (the thing users came for) are squeezed into a narrow two-column rail where the neighborhood line truncates mid-word: 'Bend, OR 97702 · Broken T…' and 'Bend, OR 97701 · Snowber…' (search-desktop-01.png). Losing the subdivision name — a key differentiator in Bend — hurts scannability of the primary content.
findings.fix: Give the rail more width (or drop to a single roomier column at this breakpoint) and let the city·subdivision line wrap to a second line or drop the subdivision cleanly rather than truncating it mid-word.

findings.title: Mobile sticky bar says 'Your broker' to anonymous visitors; desktop says 'Talk to a broker'
findings.evidence: The mobile sticky contact bar reads 'YOUR BROKER — Matt' (listing-detail-mobile-06/10/15/18.png), while the desktop card reads the neutral 'TALK TO A BROKER — Questions about this home?' with Paul Stevenson (listing-detail-desktop-02.png). ListingMobileContactBar.client.tsx line 54 hardcodes 'Your broker', directly contradicting ListingBrokerCTA.client.tsx's own comment that the card 'never says your broker'. For a first-time anonymous visitor there is no assigned broker (this is a third-party Keller Williams listing), and the broker is randomly assigned client-side (ListingBrokerCTA line 106), so the two surfaces even show different people (Paul vs Matt).
findings.fix: Change the mobile bar eyebrow from 'Your broker' to the same neutral label the desktop card uses ('Talk to a broker' / 'Questions about this home?') so both surfaces match and the copy doesn't imply a relationship the visitor doesn't have.

findings.title: Two full-width sections promise data but only say 'on request'
findings.evidence: listing-detail-desktop-09/10.png: 'CLIMATE RISK' renders only the sentence 'Detailed scoring for this property is on request' plus a GET THE CLIMATE REPORT link, and 'VACATION RENTAL' renders only 'A custom projection for this property is on request' plus GET THE RENTAL PROJECTION. page.tsx passes risk={null} and projection={null}, so these two stacked, equally-weighted sections deliver no actual data for this home — a content-less teaser pair on a 748 sqft mid-market house (vacation-rental projection is also a questionable fit for this property).
findings.fix: Only render these blocks when real per-property data exists; otherwise fold the 'request a report' asks into one compact CTA rather than stacking multiple empty teaser sections that read as filler and undercut the page's otherwise data-rich, transparent feel.

findings.title: Lead 'Featured Homes' card renders a solid black broken image
findings.evidence: listing-luxury-desktop-12.png: directly under the 'FEATURED HOMES' heading the first and largest card ($8,750,000, 19100 Macalpine Loop, The Highlands at Broken Top) is a pure black rectangle where the hero photo should be. The remaining featured cards on -13/-14 load fine, so this card's image failed with no placeholder, leading the cross-sell module with a broken tile.
findings.fix: Add an image onError fallback (brand placeholder or skip cards with no resolvable photo) to the featured-homes card so a missing photo never renders as a black box, and prefer a card that has media for the lead slot.

findings.title: '1,440.6% above the Bend median' reads as a comical outlier stat on a luxury listing
findings.evidence: listing-luxury-desktop-06.png: the Bend Market panel states 'This home is listed at $11,900,000 — 1,440.6% above the Bend median.' A four-digit percentage is technically true but tonally jarring for a trophy property and frames it as a freak outlier rather than useful context.
findings.fix: Above a threshold, drop the percent-above-median sentence or express it as a multiple ('about 15x the Bend median'); cap or suppress the figure when it exceeds a sane percentage. Target components/listing/AreaMarketContext.tsx.

findings.title: Lifestyle grid mixes grayscale and color photos
findings.evidence: In sell-desktop-12.png the 'Why buyers come here' 8-tile grid renders Snowboarding and Paddleboarding as black-and-white photos while the other six (Trail running, Skiing, Rock climbing, Golf, Hiking, Camping) are full color. The mismatch reads as a broken/unfinished asset rather than a deliberate treatment. LifestyleStrip.tsx applies no CSS filter, so the grayscale comes from the source images in the pool served by getLifestyleImages.
findings.fix: Swap the two black-and-white assets (snowboarding, paddleboarding) in the lifestyle image pool for color versions so all eight tiles share one treatment; or, if a monochrome look is wanted, apply grayscale uniformly to every tile.

findings.title: Fee/pricing message repeats across ~6 sections, stretching the page
findings.evidence: The same 2.5%/3%/3.5% plan structure and 'commission is negotiable, every listing agreement is its own conversation' / 'no follow-up beyond two emails' messaging appears in the plan explorer (sell-desktop-03), the compare table footer (sell-desktop-06), the commission prose and cards (sell-desktop-07/08), the valuation CTA (sell-desktop-13), and the FAQ (sell-desktop-14). The body runs 14 full desktop screens before the FAQ, pushing the closing CTA far down and diluting the single ask.
findings.fix: Consolidate: keep the interactive plan explorer + compare table as the one canonical pricing block and cut the near-verbatim restatements in SellCommission and the FAQ to a single cross-reference. Tightening the stack shortens time-to-CTA for the high-intent seller.

findings.title: Hero photo is a washed-out, grainy dusk shot with large mobile dead space
findings.evidence: In sell-desktop-01.png the hero image is a hazy, low-contrast pink/purple Cascades-at-dusk frame with visible grain, reading as a muted stock photo rather than a confident brand banner. On sell-mobile-01.png roughly the top 40% of the first screen is empty pink sky above the headline before any content appears. The image is chosen from the surface pool via getSurfaceImage in app/sell/page.tsx (fallback Old Mill), so this specific frame is swappable.
findings.fix: Pin the hero to a sharper, higher-contrast approved frame (e.g. the canonical Old Mill master already referenced as OLD_MILL_HERO) and bottom-anchor/crop the focal point on mobile so the headline and address form sit higher instead of below a band of empty sky.

findings.title: Hero eyebrow and lead paragraph are low-contrast over the photo
findings.evidence: In sell-desktop-01.png and sell-mobile-01.png the eyebrow 'SELL WITH RYAN REALTY' is faint light-grey on the pink sky and the value-prop lead ('Professional photography, a 3D tour, the MLS and every national feed...') is muted grey over the dark lower third of the hero image, sitting near the legibility floor for the copy that explains what the service includes.
findings.fix: Lighten the hero supporting copy to white/near-white and add a subtle bottom scrim behind the lead paragraph (or move it onto a solid panel) so both the eyebrow and the include-list read clearly on any hero frame.

findings.title: Compare-line-by-line table shows only one plan column on mobile
findings.evidence: sell-mobile-06.png shows the 'Compare line by line' table collapsed to a single Enhanced (3%) column controlled by the 2.5%/3%/3.5% toggle. A seller must repeatedly toggle back and forth to compare tiers, defeating the side-by-side purpose the desktop table (sell-desktop-04.png) delivers at a glance.
findings.fix: On mobile, render the feature rows with all three plans as compact side-by-side check/dash columns (narrower cells), or offer a two-plan compare view, so a seller can weigh tiers without toggling.

findings.title: No human or social proof anywhere near the lead form — trust rests entirely on microcopy
findings.evidence: The form asks for address, email, and phone (sell-valuation-desktop-02.png / sell-valuation-mobile-02.png) but the only credibility signals on the whole page are the one-line reassurance under the button ('A broker emails your written valuation within 24 hours... No obligation') and the license text in the footer (sell-valuation-desktop-04.png). The 'How we value your home' section (sell-valuation-desktop-03.png) explains methodology but shows no broker face, name attribution, review, or track-record stat. The brand has three normalized broker headshots available, yet none appear on a page where the visitor is handing over personal contact data.
findings.fix: Add one concrete proof element adjacent to the form: the handling broker's headshot + 'Matt Ryan, Principal Broker' attribution, or a short client testimonial, or a factual stat (e.g. homes sold / valued in Central Oregon). Keep it factual per brand voice — a real face and a real number, not adjectives.

findings.title: Property-address field is a bare text input with no autocomplete — raises typo risk on the single most important input
findings.evidence: The 'Property address *' field renders only a placeholder ('123 Main St, Bend, OR 97701') with no address suggestions (sell-valuation-desktop-02.png, sell-valuation-mobile-02.png). Source confirms it is a plain <Input type='text' autoComplete='street-address'> with no Places/autocomplete integration (app/home-valuation/ValuationForm.tsx lines 56-64). Address accuracy directly determines whether the broker can pull the right comps; a free-typed, mistyped, or ambiguous address is a silent conversion/quality drag.
findings.fix: Wire the address field to Google Places autocomplete (the site is already standardized on Google Maps) so users pick a validated address, reducing typos and speeding entry. Fall back to free text if no match.

findings.title: Hero eyebrow and top headline line sit over bright, unscrimmed photo — marginal legibility
findings.evidence: On desktop the cream eyebrow 'FREE HOME VALUATION' and the upper H1 line 'WHAT'S YOUR' render over the bright green forest and lit river of the Old Mill aerial with no darkening scrim in that zone (sell-valuation-desktop-01.png). Cream-on-bright-green is low contrast; the eyebrow in particular is hard to read. The lower part of the hero has a subtle gradient so the subhead and CTA read fine — only the top band is exposed.
findings.fix: Extend the hero's bottom-anchored scrim upward as a full-height gradient, or add a text-shadow to the eyebrow and H1, so the cream text clears contrast over the brightest part of the photo.

findings.title: 'How we value your home' cards have near-invisible borders on the white surface
findings.evidence: The three explainer cards (Local comps / Market trends / Your property) sit on a near-white background with a border so faint it barely registers, so they read as three floating text columns rather than defined cards (sell-valuation-desktop-03.png; the border is only faintly visible on mobile at sell-valuation-mobile-04.png). This under-defines them relative to the design-system card treatment used elsewhere on the site.
findings.fix: Give the cards the standard design-system card definition (visible border-border and/or shadow-sm on the bg-card surface) so they read as discrete cards.

findings.title: Footer 'Let's talk' closer's primary CTA links back to the page the user is already on
findings.evidence: The large closing band reads 'LET'S TALK.' with a primary button 'WHAT'S MY HOME WORTH →' (sell-valuation-desktop-04.png / sell-valuation-desktop-05.png, and sell-valuation-mobile-05.png). On /sell/valuation that CTA points back to the valuation page itself — a circular closer that offers the visitor no new next step after they have scrolled the whole page.
findings.fix: On this route, point the closer's primary CTA at a genuinely forward action (e.g. anchor it to the form higher on the page, or swap to 'Our selling plan' / 'Contact us'), so the big closing moment doesn't route back to the current page.

findings.title: Primary CTA appears in two different colors (orange hero vs navy final/sticky)
findings.evidence: The hero's primary button is bright orange 'Get my home value →' (desktop-01, mobile-01), but the identical final-section button is navy (desktop-06, desktop-07) and the mobile sticky bottom bar 'GET MY HOME VALUE' is also navy (mobile-01/06/09). The same conversion action has no single, recognizable color, so the bottom CTA reads as visually weaker exactly where a scrolled-down user re-decides.
findings.fix: Pick one primary-action color and use it for every instance of the 'Get my home value' button (hero, final section, sticky bar). If orange is kept for contrast against the navy hero panel, carry it through to the final CTA too.

findings.title: 'Recently sold nearby' proof is all $1M+ while the page's own median is $728K
findings.evidence: The market strip states a $728,000 median sale price (desktop-03), but every 'Recently Sold Nearby' comp shown is luxury: $1,715,000, $1,191,000, and $1,030,000 (desktop-05, mobile-06). After the hero promises a number for 'homes like yours,' a median-priced Bend homeowner sees only million-dollar homes and reads the proof as unrepresentative of their situation.
findings.fix: Include at least one or two closed comps near the market median (e.g. a $600K–$800K sale) so a typical homeowner sees a home like theirs, not only high-end sales.

findings.title: CMA sample card renders every value as '$—', reading as a broken/empty widget
findings.evidence: The 'Your Street, Your Comps' card shows 'Comparable sale 1 $—', '$—', '$—' and 'YOUR ADJUSTED VALUE $—' (desktop-03, mobile-04). The only cue that it is illustrative is a small 'Sample layout · your report carries the live figures' caption below (desktop-04). Skim-reading users see a card full of empty dashes and perceive a loading error rather than a demonstration of the deliverable.
findings.fix: Populate the sample card with clearly-labeled example figures (grayed 'example' styling) so it visually demonstrates what the report delivers instead of showing empty placeholders.

findings.title: Display headings crowd together when they wrap to two lines
findings.evidence: Amboqia display headings use very tight leading, so wrapped lines nearly collide: 'WHAT YOU'RE PROBABLY / WONDERING' on desktop-05, 'RECENTLY SOLD / NEARBY' on mobile-06, and 'READY FOR YOUR / NUMBER?' on mobile-09 have ascenders/descenders touching between the two lines. It reads but looks cramped and slightly undercuts the polish of an otherwise premium hero treatment.
findings.fix: Increase line-height on wrapped display (H2) headings so two-line headers have clear separation between rows.

findings.title: "Meet the team" section shows no people — just a heading and a lone button
findings.evidence: about-desktop-05.png: the section renders the eyebrow "Who you work with", the display heading "MEET THE TEAM" (floated far right), a divider, then a single navy "MEET THE FULL TEAM →" button on the left, followed by a large empty gap before the next section. No broker faces or names appear. On the one page whose entire job is trust, and where all eight reviews repeatedly name "Matt Ryan", a normal visitor who came specifically to see WHO they'd work with sees an empty block that reads as unfinished. Source app/about/page.tsx lines 282-298 intentionally stripped the KbTeam grid (design-audit #169) to point at /team, but that leaves this section content-thin.
findings.fix: Render a compact inline row of the three brokers (Matt Ryan, Paul Stevenson, Rebecca Ryser Peterson) using the existing transparent headshots at design_system/ryan-realty/assets/team (mirrored at public/images/brokers/*.png) with names + roles, and keep the "Meet the full team →" link below it. Faces on the About page carry more trust than a click-through.

findings.title: All three "Guides and insights" blog cards show the identical Old Mill District photo
findings.evidence: about-desktop-06.png and about-mobile-08.png: the three market-report cards ("Bend Oregon Market Report: July 2026", "Central Oregon...", "Redmond...") each render the exact same Old Mill District aerial (three smokestacks + pond), with the same JUL 10, 2026 date and near-identical titles. Three byte-identical thumbnails side by side read as a templating bug and cheapen the section on a page meant to build credibility. Source: KbArticles maps p.heroImageUrl from getRecentBlogPosts (app/about/page.tsx line 183); the three posts share one hero image.
findings.fix: Give each market-report post a distinct hero image — the per-city photography already exists in public/images/kb/ (bend-drake-park-aerial.jpg, redmond-downtown-aerial.jpg, etc.). Either set distinct heroImageUrl per post at the blog-data layer or fall back to varied town imagery in KbArticles when hero images collide.

findings.title: Mobile hero CTAs both render as filled buttons, flattening the primary/secondary distinction
findings.evidence: about-desktop-01.png shows "BROWSE →" as a solid white button and "HOME WORTH?" as an outlined (transparent, white-border) secondary. about-mobile-01.png shows BOTH as solid cream/white filled buttons, so the two hero actions read as equal weight and the intended hierarchy is lost on the viewport where it matters most.
findings.fix: Preserve the outlined secondary style for the "Home worth?" hero CTA at mobile breakpoints in KbHero.client so "Browse" stays the visually primary action.

findings.title: "By the numbers" ledger shows undecodable license numbers with no "License" label
findings.evidence: team-desktop-02.png: under the caption "BY THE NUMBERS" the right column lists each broker beside a giant tabular value "OR 201206613", "OR 201254727", "OR 201259123" — no word "License" anywhere. The caption is hardcoded generic in KbAbout.tsx (line 49, 'By the numbers', the same block used for market stats on city pages) and fed values built as `OR ${b.licenseNumber}` in app/team/page.tsx (line 116). A normal user reads "By the numbers" as an achievement/stats block, then sees numbers that mean nothing to them; "OR" even scans as the word "or." The intended trust credential (Oregon license) is lost.
findings.fix: Make the values self-describing regardless of the shared caption: prefix each with "License" (e.g. "OR License #201206613") in app/team/page.tsx brokerFacts. Better, add an optional `ledgerCap` prop to KbAbout and pass "Licensed Oregon brokers" here so the caption names the credential instead of promising stats.

findings.title: Broker cards give nothing to choose between the three brokers
findings.evidence: team-desktop-03.png and team-mobile-04.png: each card in the "Work with us" grid shows only photo, name, role (Principal Broker / Broker / Broker), a phone number, and "Work with [name] →". The grid is the whole reason a team page exists, yet a first-time user deciding who to call gets no bio, specialty, or differentiator. Source: KbTeam.client.tsx BROKERS array (lines 13-17) carries only name/role/slug/img/phone.
findings.fix: Add a one-line specialty/bio field per broker to the BROKERS array in KbTeam.client.tsx and render it under the role (e.g. buyer vs. seller focus, areas, or a short credential line), so a visitor can pick a broker with confidence.

findings.title: Ledger and card grid disagree on Rebecca's name and on broker order
findings.evidence: team-desktop-02.png lists "REBECCA RYSER PETERSON · BROKER" in the order Matt, Rebecca, Paul (from getBrokers().fullName via the page.tsx RANK sort). team-desktop-03.png shows the cards as "Rebecca Peterson" in the order Matt, Paul, Rebecca (hardcoded in KbTeam.client.tsx lines 14-16). Two on-page lists of the same three people that disagree on both a name and the ordering reads like two data sources and subtly erodes trust.
findings.fix: Pull the card names from the same broker record as the ledger (or align both to one canonical display name) and match the ordering — either update the hardcoded KbTeam array to Matt/Rebecca/Paul with "Rebecca Ryser Peterson", or feed KbTeam the ordered getBrokers() list so both sections stay in sync.

findings.title: Same "one broker, no hand-offs" claim repeated near-verbatim four times
findings.evidence: The identical promise appears in the hero lead "No hand-offs, no transaction desk, no junior agent learning on your deal" (team-desktop-01.png), twice more in the About block "No hand-offs to a junior agent, no transaction desk... The broker who prices your home is the one who answers your calls" (team-desktop-02.png), and again as FAQ answer #1 "no hand-off to a junior agent or a transaction desk, and the broker who prices your home is the one who answers your calls" (team-desktop-06.png). By the third restatement the reader learns nothing new and the page feels padded.
findings.fix: Keep the claim strong in the hero, then vary or trim the About paragraphs and FAQ answer so each section adds a new fact (e.g. what the listing gets, coverage areas) rather than re-asserting the same sentence.

findings.title: Every featured card repeats the city name in its meta line
findings.evidence: In team-member-desktop-04.png cards read 'Sold May 2026 · Bend 97707 · Vandevert Ranch · Bend' and 'Sold Sep 2025 · Bend 97702 · Sun Meadow · Bend'; team-member-desktop-05.png shows 'Sold Aug 2025 · Bend 97703 · Forest Hills · Bend' — the city renders twice on every tile. Root cause: brokerageTileToFeatured() in page.tsx builds `cityParts = [City, PostalCode]` into `sub`, then KbFeatured.client.tsx lines 128-131 append `it.city` again after `it.sub`.
findings.fix: Drop `City` from `cityParts` in brokerageTileToFeatured (keep zip + subdivision in sub, let the component append the city once), or stop appending `it.city` in KbFeatured when `it.sub` already contains it.

findings.title: 'Text Matt' and 'Email Matt' render as invisible cream-on-cream buttons
findings.evidence: In team-member-desktop-08.png the 'Work with Matt' block shows 'CALL MATT →' as a filled navy button, but 'TEXT MATT' and 'EMAIL MATT' appear as bare uppercase text with no border or fill. page.tsx gives Call `className="btn alt"` (navy fill) but Text/Email `className="btn"`; on this cream section (`background: var(--cream)`) kb.css `.btn` is cream fill + cream border + navy text, so both buttons are the same color as the background and read as non-clickable labels. Text and email are often the preferred contact channels, and here they have zero affordance.
findings.fix: Give Text/Email a navy-outline variant on cream surfaces (e.g. a `.btn.ghost`-style navy border, matching the outlined 'BROWSE HOMES' button in the Let's Talk footer) so all three contact actions read as buttons.

findings.title: SMS consent checkbox sits below the submit button and its choice isn't captured
findings.evidence: In team-member-desktop-08.png the 'I agree to receive text messages...' consent checkbox renders BELOW the 'Request my valuation' submit button — reversed from the expected read order (agree, then submit). Worse: LeadCaptureBlock.tsx renders <SmsConsentDisclosure/> (line 313) with no `checked`/`onCheckedChange`, while handleSubmit posts the typed React `state` object (which has no smsConsent field), not FormData — so the user's checkbox state is never recorded for submitBrokerSellerLead. SmsConsentDisclosure.tsx's own doc warns this must be passed on state-based forms. The TCPA/A2P consent appears functional but is decorative on this page.
findings.fix: Move the consent block above the submit button, and thread the checkbox through props: pass `checked`/`onCheckedChange` into SmsConsentDisclosure, add `smsConsent` to the payload, and forward it to submitBrokerSellerLead so consent is actually captured.

findings.title: Two stacked home-valuation asks, the top one bounces the user off Matt's page
findings.evidence: team-member-desktop-07.png stacks two valuation entry points: the KbSell band 'WHAT'S YOUR HOME WORTH?' with an address input + 'VALUE MY HOME →', immediately above the 'Get a valuation from Matt' form (the broker-attributed lead capture). Per page.tsx's own comment (lines 416-421) the KbSell CTA redirects to the generic /sell/valuation page, so a visitor who uses the prominent top address bar is navigated away from Matt's page and the broker-attributed form below, losing the 'from Matt' framing and attribution.
findings.fix: On the broker page, point the KbSell CTA at the on-page form (anchor-scroll to the LeadCaptureBlock) instead of /sell/valuation, or drop the KbSell address band here so the broker-attributed 'Get a valuation from Matt' form is the single, unambiguous valuation path.

findings.title: Contact form sits entirely below a full-viewport hero — the page's one action isn't visible on load
findings.evidence: contact-desktop-01.png is 100% hero photo + 'CONTACT US' heading with zero form visible; the form only appears in contact-desktop-02.png. contact-mobile-01.png is the same — the full mobile viewport is the Old Mill photo with the headline crammed into the bottom ~25%, and the form doesn't appear until contact-mobile-02.png. Source: app/contact/page.tsx renders a full-height KbHero (KbHero.client.tsx) above the #contact-form section, with only a 'Send a message' jump CTA.
findings.fix: On /contact, either render ContactForm inside the hero via KbHero's existing `formSlot` prop (the same slot pattern used for the /sell address-capture form — see KbHero.client.tsx lines 68-73, 237) so the fields are above the fold, or cap the hero to ~55-60vh so the top of the form card is visible on load. Keep the 'Send a message' jump CTA as a fallback.

findings.title: Secondary 'Office / Ryan Realty' column out-weighs the primary form column on desktop
findings.evidence: In contact-desktop-02.png the right (secondary) column opens with a large Amboqia display heading 'Ryan Realty' (app/contact/page.tsx line 206, clamp up to 3.2rem), while the left (primary) form column is topped only by the tiny grey 'Send a message' sec-index label (line 162). The eye lands first on the big 'Ryan Realty' wordmark rather than on the form, which is the page's actual conversion action.
findings.fix: Give the form column a display-weight heading comparable to the office block — e.g. an Amboqia H2 like 'Send us a message' above the fields — so the primary action anchors the section instead of the office info. Mobile stacks form-first so it is unaffected; scope the heading bump to the desktop two-column layout.

findings.title: Featured city cards with zero inventory show bare '—' for both stats, reading as broken data
findings.evidence: Tumalo (cities-desktop-05.png) and Crooked River Ranch (cities-desktop-08.png) get full editorial treatment — large hero photo, big Amboqia name, description sentence, and 'Homes for sale / Open houses' links — but their stat band shows only two short dashes above 'ACTIVE' and 'MEDIAN LIST', with no days stat and no market-verdict pill. On a page whose hero promises 'Live inventory and pricing from the regional MLS, refreshed through the day' (cities-desktop-01.png), a lone '—' reads as a data-load failure, not as intentional zero inventory. app/cities/page.tsx line 363 renders '—' when activeCount is 0, so the code comment's stated intent of an 'honest 0 active card' is not actually achieved — the user sees an ambiguous dash, never the number 0 or any explanation.
findings.fix: Replace the bare em-dash for zero-inventory featured cities with explicit microcopy such as 'No active listings right now' (and hide the empty median cell), or demote Tumalo and Crooked River Ranch into the 'Smaller towns on the ledger' list where a missing count is not jarring.

findings.title: The browse-to-listings action ('Homes for sale') is a small text link with the same weight as a redundant 'guide' link
findings.evidence: On every featured city row (e.g. Bend, cities-desktop-02.png) the two dominant interactive targets — the large photo and the big city name — both link to /cities/[slug] (the city guide), per app/cities/page.tsx lines 315-347. The actual browse-inventory path, 'Homes for sale', is a 14px bold text link (line 421) sitting in a three-link row alongside '[City] guide' (which is redundant with the card click that already goes to the guide) and 'Open houses', all at equal weight. On a discovery hub whose core job is getting a user into listings, the money action competes visually with a duplicate link instead of standing out.
findings.fix: Drop the redundant '[City] guide' text link (the whole card already opens the guide) and give 'Homes for sale' a button/pill treatment or a 'View {active} homes →' affordance so the browse-listings path is the obvious next step.

findings.title: Stat labels use real-estate jargon a non-expert can't parse
findings.evidence: City cards label the days figure 'ACTIVE LISTINGS' MEDIAN AGE' (cities-desktop-02.png, '53 DAYS / ACTIVE LISTINGS' MEDIAN AGE') and the hero's third stat is 'MONTHS OF SUPPLY' (cities-desktop-01.png). A normal buyer/seller does not know what 'active listings' median age' or 'months of supply' mean; only the plain-language verdict pill ('Buyer's market' / 'Balanced market') is decodable. The verbose age label was widened deliberately to disambiguate from the detail page (per the comment in page.tsx lines 379-385), but the result is harder for a first-time visitor to read.
findings.fix: Relabel to plain language, e.g. 'Typical days on market' for the age stat, and keep the verdict pill as the human summary; consider a small tooltip on 'Months of supply'.

findings.title: 12 full-size editorial rows with no in-page city picker means a long scroll to reach a specific town
findings.evidence: The featured section stacks 12 large alternating photo/content rows (cities-desktop-02.png through cities-desktop-08.png) before the compact ledger and CTA. A visitor who already knows they want, say, Culver or Prineville must scroll past seven or more full rows to find it — there is no jump list, filter, or city-chip nav at the top of the section (app/cities/page.tsx lines 299-442).
findings.fix: Add a sticky row of city name chips (or an A–Z/quick-jump index) at the top of the 'Where do you want to live?' section that anchors to each city row, so users can jump straight to the town they care about.

findings.title: "Latest market activity" live feed badges every item NEW but dates are stale, out of order, and future-dated
findings.evidence: city-bend-mobile-15.png: the module is titled 'LATEST MARKET ACTIVITY', flagged 'LIVE · MLS · 8 UPDATES', and every row carries a 'NEW' badge, yet the dates read MAY 1, MAY 15, JUL 14, JUN 8, JUL 6 top-to-bottom. They are not sorted newest-first, span 2.5 months, and one (JUL 14) is dated after the current day (Jul 12). A 'live/latest' feed that shows 10-week-old items all labeled 'NEW' in random order undercuts the freshness claim it's making.
findings.fix: Sort the feed strictly newest-first, reserve the 'NEW' badge for items inside a genuinely recent window (e.g. last 7–14 days), and confirm the date field being displayed (list date vs status-change date) so no future dates surface.

findings.title: Mobile guide-card headline clips mid-line and overlaps the body paragraph
findings.evidence: city-bend-mobile-18.png: the display headline 'BEND CONSIDERS WILDFIRE-RESISTANT BUILDING STANDARDS…' shows the ellipsis on line 3 but a garbled, half-cut 4th line still bleeds through underneath it and collides with the top of the 'Bend City Council met April 1, 2026…' paragraph. The clamp isn't cutting cleanly, so the heading looks corrupted.
findings.fix: Apply a proper line-clamp to the card's display heading (-webkit-line-clamp with overflow:hidden and a line-height that fits the clamp) so it truncates to N full lines with the ellipsis and no partial line, and add margin between the heading and the body paragraph.

findings.title: Featured Homes lead tile loads as a solid-black block with a default spinner instead of a branded skeleton
findings.evidence: city-bend-desktop-05.png shows the first tile directly under the 'FEATURED HOMES' heading as a full-width pure-black rectangle with a thin default loading-circle in its center (it resolves to the $5,995,000 tile in city-bend-desktop-06.png). city-bend-mobile-06.png shows the same black block beginning at the bottom. On a slower connection this leaves a large unbranded black void as the first thing under the section title.
findings.fix: Use the site's skeleton/blurhash placeholder for featured tiles while the image decodes rather than a bare black container with a browser spinner.

findings.title: Golf/master-planned community row shows "Vandevert Ranch — 0 ACTIVE" as a tappable dead-end
findings.evidence: city-bend-desktop-12.png lists 'Vandevert Ranch' in the Golf and Master-Planned Communities ledger with '0 ACTIVE'. Tapping a 0-listing row routes to an empty results page, a dead-end in the browse flow.
findings.fix: Hide communities with 0 active listings from the ledger, or keep the row but replace the link target with a 'none active right now — see nearby / notify me' state instead of an empty listing page.

findings.title: Community photos misrepresent the place — foreign alpine shot and wrong-location filler
findings.evidence: Mountain High (a Bend neighborhood) is illustrated with a jagged snow-peak-above-a-sea-of-clouds image that reads as the Alps, captioned 'Area view · Bend' (communities-desktop-12, mobile-15) — served by the unconstrained getSurfaceImages('hero') pool (page.tsx lines 140-144, 303-305). Pronghorn — described as 'high desert, northeast of Bend off Powell Butte Highway' — shows the Old Mill District downtown-Bend riverfront with the three smokestacks and NO 'Area view' label, presented as the community itself (communities-desktop-04); that same Old Mill image reappears (labeled) on Mt Bachelor Village (communities-desktop-10). A local buyer instantly recognizes these as the wrong place, undermining a brokerage whose pitch is local expertise.
findings.fix: Audit the curated communityImage() mappings (Pronghorn resolves to an Old Mill photo) and constrain the hero fallback pool to verified Central Oregon photography. Use a real community/local photo per row; never show an out-of-region landscape under a 'Bend' label, and don't reuse one city photo across multiple communities.

findings.title: Per-card action links have no resting affordance (hover-only underline, dead on touch)
findings.evidence: Each community card's two actions — '{name} guide' and 'Homes for sale in {city}' — are bold navy text styled `underline-offset-4 hover:underline` (page.tsx lines 372-385), so they only underline on hover. At rest (communities-desktop-02, -04, -10; mobile-10) they read as bold labels indistinguishable from the 'City · Oregon' sublabel, and on mobile hover never fires, so the card's primary next-steps never signal they're clickable.
findings.fix: Give the links a persistent affordance: apply a resting underline (or render them with a trailing arrow / as a small button), instead of hover-only, so they read as tappable on first glance and on touch.

findings.title: Featured-homes flagship media loads as a full-bleed black void with a spinner
findings.evidence: community-tetherow-desktop-02.png: below the cream "FEATURED HOMES" title the flagship poster area renders as a near-full-viewport pure-black rectangle with only a thin loading ring in the center. community-tetherow-desktop-03.png shows the same slot once loaded (the $4,000,000 Hardin Martin Court photo). The hero featured image is loading="lazy" with no immediate poster/skeleton (components/site/kb/KbFeatured.client.tsx), so on scroll/slower connections the highest-value module first paints as a broken-looking black block.
findings.fix: Eager-load the first (hero) featured image and give .lst-media a cream skeleton or blurred low-res poster instead of a bare dark container, so the flagship listing paints on arrival rather than as a black void with a spinner.

findings.title: Area-guide video sits small and centered in a wide navy band with large empty margins
findings.evidence: community-tetherow-desktop-14.png: the "Watch Tetherow" clip renders at roughly half the content width, centered inside a full-width navy box with wide empty navy on both sides (and above/below). Cause: components/site/kb/KbAreaGuideVideo.tsx caps the wide cut at maxHeight:70vh with a fixed aspect-ratio 16/9, so on wide desktop the height cap shrinks the width and flex-centering leaves large dead navy space, plus raw native <video> controls look unbranded against the otherwise polished editorial layout.
findings.fix: Let the wide 16/9 cut fill the content column (remove or raise the maxHeight:70vh cap and constrain by container width instead) so the video spans the band rather than pillarboxing into centered dead navy.

findings.title: Map section H2 duplicates the hero H1 verbatim ("Tetherow Homes For Sale")
findings.evidence: community-tetherow-desktop-01.png shows the hero H1 "TETHEROW HOMES FOR SALE"; community-tetherow-desktop-04.png shows the map section's giant display title as the identical "TETHEROW HOMES FOR SALE" (eyebrow "Tetherow," subtitle about clicking dots). Repeating the exact page H1 as a second full-size display heading dilutes the hero and gives the map block a title that doesn't describe what the block is.
findings.fix: Retitle the map section to describe its own content, e.g. "On the map" or "Tetherow on the map," and reserve the "Homes for sale" headline for the hero only.

findings.title: Membership tiles repeat "Ask the club · 844-431-9701" six times
findings.evidence: community-tetherow-desktop-11.png: across the three membership cards (Golf / Sport / Social) both the Initiation and Monthly dues rows all read "Ask the club · 844-431-9701" — six identical lines. It's honest but visually repetitive and low-information; the same number also repeats in the "Membership office: 844-431-9701" footer below.
findings.fix: Collapse the pricing rows to a single per-tier line (e.g. "Initiation + dues — on request") and surface the phone number once per card or only in the footer, so the tiles read as differentiated tiers rather than a wall of the same phone number.

findings.title: Market module stacks $2,250,000 (Tetherow list) directly above a $743,000 (Bend) chart
findings.evidence: community-tetherow-desktop-06.png: the module leads with "$2,250,000 MEDIAN LIST PRICE" and immediately below shows a trend line reading "$743,000 · MEDIAN SALE · BEND (CITY)" with a low-contrast grey disclaimer "Too few recent sales here for a standalone trend. This line tracks Bend (city)." A skimming buyer sees two very different large dollar figures for "Tetherow" and can't quickly tell which is the real local price; the explanatory line is easy to miss at that contrast.
findings.fix: Raise the disclaimer's prominence/contrast and label the chart's scope inline near the $743K value (e.g. a visible "Bend citywide" tag on the number), so the magnitude gap reads as two clearly different scopes rather than a contradiction.

findings.title: All three market-report cards use the identical Bend Old Mill photo
findings.evidence: housing-market-desktop-04.png shows the 'Bend', 'Central Oregon', and 'Redmond' July 2026 Market Report cards side by side, each illustrated with the exact same Old Mill District (three-smokestacks) drone shot; mobile-04.png confirms Bend and Central Oregon reuse it. Rendered from p.heroImageUrl via getRecentBlogPosts (page.tsx L235 → KbArticles.tsx). Three identical images — and a Bend landmark standing in for the Redmond report — reads as templated placeholder art and undercuts the page's whole 'live, specific, local data' credibility.
findings.fix: Give each market-report blog_posts row a geography-distinct hero image (Bend / Central Oregon / Redmond), or dedupe inside KbArticles so no two adjacent cards share an image and a Bend landmark is never used for a Redmond report.

findings.title: Zero-inventory city (Tumalo) renders at full weight with a blank median
findings.evidence: housing-market-desktop-03.png shows 'Tumalo' in the giant editorial ledger with '0 ACTIVE' and no median value, sitting directly between 'La Pine 175 · $500,000' and 'Terrebonne 7 · $700,000'. The empty price line at identical type weight reads as a broken/missing-data row rather than an intentional 'no listings right now' state. Deliberate per page.tsx L216-226 (zero-active cities pushed with medianPrice: null).
findings.fix: For zero-active tiles, render an explicit muted 'No active listings' in place of the blank median in KbExploreTowns town-price branch, and/or sort zero-active cities to the bottom so they don't sit mid-ledger.

findings.title: Desktop 'Market by city' rows give no persistent cue that they are links
findings.evidence: housing-market-desktop-02.png and -03.png show Redmond/Bend/Sisters/Sunriver as a static-looking stats table with no arrow, chevron, or underline at rest. In KbExploreTowns.client.tsx each row is a full <a> to /housing-market/<city>, but the '.town-arr' affordance is shown only on hover:none (touch); desktop relies on a hover photo-reveal, so at first glance a visitor may not realize the per-city market pages are reachable here — the hub's core navigation job.
findings.fix: Expose a subtle persistent affordance on hover-capable desktop too (show the row arrow at rest or add a hover row-background/underline), instead of gating '.town-arr' to hover:none only.

findings.title: Home-valuation prompt repeats three times, two near-identical modules back to back
findings.evidence: The 'what's my home worth' ask appears in the hero as a 'HOME WORTH?' button (housing-market-desktop-01.png), again as the full-height 'WHAT'S YOUR HOME WORTH?' split module (housing-market-desktop-06.png / KbSell), and a third time in the footer 'LET'S TALK / WHAT'S MY HOME WORTH' block (housing-market-desktop-08.png). KbSell and the footer LET'S TALK are two near-identical valuation CTAs within one scroll, separated only by the broker form, making the bottom third three stacked seller asks and diluting focus.
findings.fix: Differentiate the two adjacent valuation modules — keep KbSell as the single valuation CTA and let the footer LET'S TALK lead with the buyer/browse path, so the bottom third isn't three repetitions of the same seller prompt.

findings.title: Three city guide cards all use the same Bend Old Mill photo
findings.evidence: In market-report-desktop-06.png the 'Sisters Oregon Market Report', 'Sunriver Oregon Market Report', and 'La Pine Oregon Market Report' cards render the identical Old Mill District (Bend) drone image with the three smokestacks — same framing, pond, and horizon in all three. On an authority page whose value prop is 'live, local, real' data, three identical photos labeled for three different towns reads as templated and quietly erodes credibility. The images come from p.heroImageUrl in app/housing-market/central-oregon/page.tsx:340, and the three source blog posts share one hero image.
findings.fix: Give each city market-report post a distinct hero (the town's own photography). At minimum, dedupe on this page: if heroImageUrl repeats across cards, fall back to a per-city image or a neutral brand treatment so no two adjacent cards show the same photo.

findings.title: Two back-to-back home-valuation closers repeat the same ask
findings.evidence: The bottom third stacks three closers: a 'Talk to a broker' contact form (market-report-desktop-08.png), then a 'WHAT'S YOUR HOME WORTH?' module with an address input + 'VALUE MY HOME' and the copy 'Built from what your street actually trades for' (market-report-desktop-09.png), then immediately a 'LET'S TALK' block whose copy 'Tell us the street. We bring the comps and the number it trades for' and primary button 'WHAT'S MY HOME WORTH' repeat the module directly above it (market-report-desktop-10.png). Two consecutive near-identical valuation pitches read as padding and dilute the single clear next step.
findings.fix: Collapse the redundancy: keep the functional 'What's your home worth' address module, and either drop the 'LET'S TALK' block or repurpose it as a lightweight footer band that points to browsing homes rather than re-pitching the same valuation ask.

findings.title: Tumalo shows a dead '0 ACTIVE' row with a blank median
findings.evidence: In the 'Cities and towns' list (market-report-desktop-05.png) Tumalo renders '0 ACTIVE' with no median figure beneath it, unlike every other town which shows an active count plus a '$xxx,000 median'. The empty/blank median reads as missing data on a page that markets itself on live MLS accuracy.
findings.fix: Suppress towns with 0 active listings from the list, or render an explicit 'No active listings' state instead of a blank median so the row doesn't look like a data gap.

findings.title: 'See the full market report' button on the page titled 'Market Report' is ambiguous
findings.evidence: The page H1 is 'CENTRAL OREGON MARKET REPORT' (market-report-desktop-01.png), yet mid-page a filled CTA reads 'SEE THE FULL MARKET REPORT →' (market-report-desktop-03.png). A normal reader can't tell what fuller report this leads to when they believe they're already on the market report, making the link's destination unclear.
findings.fix: Relabel the button to name its actual target, e.g. 'Read the July 2026 report' or 'See the monthly report', so the destination is unambiguous.

findings.title: Mobile review list never caps — all 24 full-height cards stack into a ~20-screen wall that buries the conversion CTA
findings.evidence: The CSS meant to cap mobile at 4 cards is dead: kb.css:1340 `.kb-root .kb-rev-card:nth-child(n+5){display:none;}` targets the <figure> element, which is always the ONLY child (child 1) of its <li> in app/reviews/page.tsx, so :nth-child(n+5) never matches. Result: reviews-mobile-13.png shows a review from Oct 2019 (Charise Millard) still rendering deep in the stack — every one of the 24 verbatim reviews renders one-per-viewport, and only after all of them do the 'Read more on Google' + 'Talk to a Ryan Realty broker / Contact us' conversion block appear. The team's own comment (kb.css:1337-1339) says the uncapped wall 'buried the sections below' — that regression is live again because the selector is broken.
findings.fix: Fix the selector to target the grid children (the <li>), not the figure: `.kb-root .kb-reviews-grid > li:nth-child(n+5){display:none;}` inside the max-width:780px block. This restores the intended 4-card mobile cap; 'Read all on Google' carries the rest.

findings.title: align-items:start grid opens a large dead zone beside unusually long reviews
findings.evidence: reviews-desktop-05.png: the 'annie jenkins' card (a very long review) is roughly 2.5x the height of its row-mates 'cason mays' (left) and 'Charise Millard' (right), which end early and leave two large empty columns of cream below them before the section ends. The grid uses align-items:start (kb.css:1327) so a single tall card defines the row height while short neighbors do not fill it.
findings.fix: Render the review grid as CSS multi-column masonry (column-count:3 with break-inside:avoid on .kb-rev-card) so cards flow to fill vertical space instead of leaving row-aligned gaps; or cap very long quotes with a 'Read full review' expansion so card heights stay closer within a row.

findings.title: Two near-identical 'reviews on Google' links sit within one screen of each other
findings.evidence: reviews-desktop-02.png shows a filled navy 'VIEW REVIEWS ON GOOGLE' button and, immediately below in the section header, a 'Read all on Google →' text link — both point to GOOGLE_REVIEWS_URL and appear within the same viewport, plus a third 'READ MORE ON GOOGLE' button at the grid foot (reviews-desktop-05.png). The top pair reads as duplicated CTAs stacked on top of each other.
findings.fix: Keep the single top 'View reviews on Google' chip (with the 5.0 · 24 aggregate) and the bottom 'Read more on Google' button; drop the redundant 'Read all on Google →' header link so the same destination isn't offered twice within one screen.

findings.title: Bylines appear on market-report cards but vanish on guide/analysis cards
findings.evidence: blog-desktop-03 shows 'MATT RYAN  JUL 10, 2026  2 MIN READ' on the Central Oregon card, but blog-desktop-04 ('Understanding Months of Supply') and blog-desktop-05 ('Price per square foot', 'Bend considers wildfire') and blog-desktop-06 ('Eagle Crest', 'Arts and Culture') show only date + read-time with no author. Source renders the author conditionally: `{post.author_name && <span>...}` (app/blog/page.tsx line 295), so posts missing author_name silently drop the byline. Inconsistent authorship looks like a data gap and weakens the authority a real-estate blog relies on.
findings.fix: Populate author_name for every published post (or fall back to a default 'Ryan Realty' / 'Matt Ryan' byline) so every card carries the same author+date+read-time metadata row.

findings.title: 'Recent posts' list at the bottom just repeats the July 2026 reports already shown up top
findings.evidence: blog-desktop-06 / blog-mobile-11 'RECENT POSTS' lists Bend, Central Oregon, Redmond, Sisters, and Sunriver July 2026 market reports — the exact same five posts already occupying the featured slot (blog-desktop-02) and the first grid cards (blog-desktop-03/04) on page 1. The section adds vertical scroll with zero new content and makes the page feel padded.
findings.fix: Exclude posts already rendered in the featured/grid section on page 1, or repurpose the block to surface popular or older evergreen posts (e.g. getPopularBlogSlugs, which is already imported) so it adds discovery value.

findings.title: Orphan 'Share' pill sits in the filter row with an ambiguous referent
findings.evidence: blog-desktop-02: a standalone 'Share' pill (upload icon) sits directly under the category-filter chips. Source shows it shares the blog index URL itself (ShareButton url=`${siteUrl}/blog`, app/blog/page.tsx lines 204-210). On an index page a lone Share control is confusing — users share individual articles, not a listing page — and its placement inside the filter toolbar makes it read like a stray filter.
findings.fix: Remove the Share control from the index (share belongs on individual post pages), or move it out of the filter row and label it explicitly (e.g. 'Share this blog').

findings.title: Article has no author byline or author bio — zero attribution on an expertise piece
findings.evidence: The meta row shows only 'JULY 20, 2025 · 7 MIN READ · [share icon]' with no author name (blog-post-desktop-01.png), and the page jumps straight from the tags/Share row to RELATED POSTS with no author-bio card (blog-post-desktop-08.png). The template in app/blog/[slug]/page.tsx renders a byline (lines 191-199) and an 'About the author' card (lines 276-322) only when post.author_name is set — it is empty for this post, so both are suppressed. A local-expertise guide published with no named human author undercuts E-E-A-T and credibility for a normal reader deciding whether to trust the brokerage.
findings.fix: Populate author_name (and author_slug) for this post so the byline links to the broker's /team page and the 'About the author' card renders. Attribute every published guide to one of the three brokers.

findings.title: Body text runs ~100+ characters per line — measure is too wide for comfortable long-form reading
findings.evidence: Paragraph lines span nearly the full 880px article column, e.g. the intro line 'The appraisal is the part of the home buying process that makes everyone nervous. A licensed appraiser, hired by your' is a single ~115-char line (blog-post-desktop-02.png; also -03, -05, -07). The prose div uses `max-w-none` (app/blog/[slug]/page.tsx line 234), which disables the typography plugin's built-in ~65ch optimal measure and lets text fill the full 880px. Optimal reading measure is 65-75 characters; this is well over it and increases eye fatigue across a 7-minute read.
findings.fix: Remove `max-w-none` from the prose div (let @tailwindcss/typography cap the text at ~65ch) or set an explicit measure of ~68ch / ~700px on the prose column while leaving the hero image full-width.

findings.title: Top share control is an unlabeled icon-only button
findings.evidence: In the header meta row the share control renders as a bare upload-arrow glyph in a white box with no text label (blog-post-desktop-01.png), from ShareButton variant='compact' (page.tsx line 211). The identical action at the bottom of the article is a labeled 'Share' button (blog-post-desktop-08.png), so the top control is the odd one out and its purpose is not self-evident to a first-time reader.
findings.fix: Add a visible 'Share' label to the compact top button (or a tooltip/aria-label surfaced on hover) so it matches the labeled bottom control.

findings.title: Five identical ghost buttons in the hero — no primary CTA at the funnel entry
findings.evidence: buy-desktop-01.png: the hero offers SEARCH HOMES, GET LISTING ALERTS, PRICE DROPS, TALK TO A BROKER, and AREA GUIDES all rendered as the same white-outline transparent 'btn ghost' (page.tsx HERO_CHIPS map, line 233 applies 'btn ghost' to every chip). On the primary buyer-funnel entry there is no visual priority, so the eye has nothing to land on and the core action (Search homes) is just one of five equal chips.
findings.fix: Promote the single core action (Search homes) to a solid/filled primary button and demote the remaining four to secondary/ghost, or trim to 2-3 actions (Search homes + Get listing alerts). One clear primary reduces decision paralysis and lifts click-through.

findings.title: Closing pre-footer CTA emphasizes the seller action over the buyer action on a buy page
findings.evidence: buy-desktop-06.png / buy-desktop-07.png: the 'LET'S TALK.' pre-footer block (rendered by the shared KbFooter, page.tsx line 445) makes 'WHAT'S MY HOME WORTH' the filled primary button and 'BROWSE HOMES' the outline secondary. A buyer who reaches the end of the buy page is nudged toward a seller home-valuation tool as the emphasized action, while the buyer-relevant Browse homes is de-emphasized. Note: this is the shared global pre-footer, so the fix likely belongs to the footer component rather than /buy alone.
findings.fix: For the buyer context (or globally, per-surface), lead the pre-footer CTA with the buyer action (Browse homes / Get listing alerts) as the filled primary and keep the valuation CTA as secondary, so the emphasized action matches the page's audience.

findings.title: Hero has no call-to-action — the first screen of a lead-gen landing ends on prose with no next step
findings.evidence: The hero (desktop-01) is eyebrow "BEND · CENTRAL OREGON", H1 "Luxury homes in Bend, Oregon", and a subhead, then nothing actionable — no button. Source page.tsx lines 91-106 confirm the hero block contains only text. A luxury buyer arriving from search sees a strong pitch but is given no explicit action (browse the homes, talk to a broker); forward motion depends on the user deciding to scroll.
findings.fix: Add one primary button in the hero, e.g. "Browse the 214 luxury homes" scrolling to / linking the listings, or "Talk to a Bend luxury broker." Keep it to a single filled Button so the first viewport signals the next step.

findings.title: Flagship listing card reads as incoherent: $11.9M for a 3 bd / 3 ba / 2,268 sqft "home"
findings.evidence: Strict price-desc sort places 65255 Swalley Road at the very top as the hero card: "$11,900,000 · 3 BD · 3 BA · 2,268 SQFT" (desktop-02). To a normal user that is an $11.9M home smaller than an average house — clearly an acreage/land-value parcel, but the card shows only living sqft, no lot size, so the number reads as a mistake and undercuts the "luxury homes" promise on the most prominent card. The code comment (page.tsx lines 50-52) shows the team already fought this class of outlier by adding propertyType='A'; land-priced residential parcels still slip to the top.
findings.fix: When list price is high relative to living area (or acreage is large), surface lot size / "X acres" in the card meta line so the price reads coherently, and/or de-prioritize sub-threshold-sqft outliers so the flagship card is a recognizable luxury home. The meta builder is at page.tsx lines 61-65.

findings.title: Giant right-aligned category headers overpower the questions they introduce
findings.evidence:
In faq-desktop-02.png the display word 'NEIGHBORHOODS' is rendered at hero scale and right-aligned, yet it introduces only 2 short, small, left-aligned questions on the far left, with a wide empty gap between header and content. 'BUYING' repeats this; faq-desktop-03.png shows 'SELLING' and 'WORKING WITH US' the same way. The decorative header is visually heavier than the actual content beneath it (the questions are the page's value). Source: app/faq/page.tsx lines 284-305 render `

{g.cat}

` per group; the code comment at 294-296 already acknowledges a prior audit about full-viewport-scale headings for as few as 2 questions.
findings.fix: Reduce the per-category header type scale and left-align it directly above its question list (or make it a compact section label), so the visual weight sits on the questions, not the decoration. Keep the giant display treatment for page-level H1s only.

findings.title: Hero CTAs are generic and off-intent for an FAQ page; four competing CTAs stack at the top
findings.evidence: faq-desktop-01.png hero shows 'BROWSE →' and 'HOME WORTH?'; faq-desktop-02.png shows a second CTA row 'TALK TO US →' and 'LATEST MARKET REPORT →' directly below. The two hero buttons are KbHero defaults (components/site/kb/KbHero.client.tsx lines 94-97: cta 'Browse' → /homes-for-sale, ctaSecondary 'Home worth?' → /sell/valuation) because app/faq/page.tsx never passes cta/ctaSecondary. A visitor who came to read answers meets four conversion buttons and none that says 'find your answer'; the bare label 'BROWSE' also doesn't say browse-what.
findings.fix: Pass page-specific cta/ctaSecondary to KbHero (the override hook already exists per the code comment at lines 60-66) — e.g. a primary 'Browse questions' that jumps to #faq-toc plus 'Talk to us' — and drop or relabel the generic 'BROWSE'/'HOME WORTH?' defaults so the top of an FAQ page serves the FAQ-reader intent.

findings.title: Page's own contact CTA sits directly on top of the near-identical footer 'Let's talk' band
findings.evidence: faq-desktop-03.png ends with the page-authored 'DID WE MISS YOUR QUESTION? … Reach out … Contact Ryan Realty' block (app/faq/page.tsx lines 308-325). faq-desktop-04.png immediately follows with the footer's full-height 'LET'S TALK … What's my home worth / Browse homes' band. Two consecutive full-width 'reach out' prompts pad the page bottom and split the single clear next step.
findings.fix: Consolidate: keep the FAQ-specific 'Did we miss your question → Contact Ryan Realty' block (it is well-targeted) and let it stand alone, or tighten it so it doesn't read as a duplicate of the immediately-following global 'Let's talk' CTA band.

findings.title: Accordion expand affordance is weak: thin far-right chevron on ultra-wide rows, nothing open by default
findings.evidence: In faq-desktop-02.png and faq-desktop-03.png every question row shows only the question text at the far left and a thin, low-contrast chevron at the extreme right edge, separated by a very wide empty gap; no answer is visible on load. FaqAccordion uses Accordion type='single' collapsible with no defaultValue (app/faq/FaqAccordion.tsx line 20), so a first-time visitor gets zero visible answers and may not register that the rows are expandable.
findings.fix: Open the first item by default (defaultValue on the first entry) to demonstrate the interaction, and/or strengthen the row affordance (full-row hover state, slightly bolder/closer chevron) so it reads as clickable across the wide desktop row.

findings.title: 'Browse by topic' reads like filter chips with counts but only anchor-jumps; no active state
findings.evidence: faq-desktop-02.png shows four bordered cells 'Neighborhoods (2) / Buying (4) / Selling (3) / Working with us (2)' styled like filter tabs with result counts, but they are plain anchor links that only scroll the page (app/faq/page.tsx lines 262-278, href='#neighborhoods' etc.). There is no selected/active state, and with all 10 questions already on one short scroll, the jump-nav's value is marginal while its filter-like appearance is ambiguous.
findings.fix: Signal these are jump links, not filters — e.g. add a small 'Jump to' affordance or anchor icon, or keep the counts but restyle so they don't read as toggleable filter chips.

findings.title: Five competing CTAs plus a search bar stack before the actual resources
findings.evidence: resources-desktop-01.png hero carries a full property search bar + BROWSE + HOME WORTH?; resources-desktop-02.png then adds a second CTA row VIEW MARKET REPORTS + SEARCH LISTINGS immediately above the 'Guides, tools and reports' grid. BROWSE and SEARCH LISTINGS both route to listings browse, and VIEW MARKET REPORTS duplicates the first grid tile 'Market reports' (both go to /housing-market/reports). The page gives no clear first action before the resource ledger.
findings.fix: Delete the standalone CTA row (View market reports / Search listings) in app/resources/page.tsx — both destinations are already reachable via the hero and the resource tiles. Let the hero present one primary action and drop the eye directly into the resource grid.

findings.title: Two identical home-valuation asks stacked back to back
findings.evidence: resources-desktop-03.png shows the standalone 'Curious what your home is worth? Get your free home valuation' card sitting directly above the footer's 'LET'S TALK … WHAT'S MY HOME WORTH' block, which repeats the same offer ('we bring the comps and the number it trades for') and the same CTA. The page adds HomeValuationCta right before KbFooter, which already leads with that ask.
findings.fix: Remove the standalone HomeValuationCta section from /resources (the footer's Let's Talk block already carries the valuation ask), or convert valuation into one tile inside the resource grid so it isn't a second full-width repeat of the same message.

findings.title: Same two actions wear three different labels each
findings.evidence: Home valuation is labeled 'HOME WORTH?' in the hero (resources-desktop-01.png), 'Get your free home valuation' in the card (resources-desktop-03.png), and 'WHAT'S MY HOME WORTH' in the Let's Talk block (resources-desktop-03.png). Browse is 'BROWSE' (01), 'SEARCH LISTINGS' (02), and 'BROWSE HOMES' (03). One destination, multiple labels — a user can't tell they lead to the same place.
findings.fix: Standardize to one verb per action across the page: 'What's my home worth' for valuation and 'Browse homes' for listings. Update the hero CTA labels and the CTA row to match.

findings.title: Hero eyebrow crowds the H1 (caps nearly touch)
findings.evidence: Zoomed crop of resources-desktop-01.png shows the eyebrow 'CENTRAL OREGON · TOOLS & MARKET DATA' sitting so tight to the display H1 that the caps of 'BUYER' rise into the eyebrow line, making the eyebrow cramped and harder to read against the photo.
findings.fix: Add a few px of margin between the eyebrow and titleTop in the KbHero layout so the small label has clear breathing room above the large Amboqia headline.

findings.title: Hero sub-line is a broken sentence fragment when the count is zero
findings.evidence: At the bottom of the hero (open-houses-desktop-01.png) the lead reads just 'across Central Oregon this week.' with no subject in front of it. page.tsx:191-200 passes `activeCount: openHouseCount || null` and `lead: 'across Central Oregon this week.'`; KbHero.client.tsx:244-254 renders the bold count prefix ('N open houses') only when `activeCount != null`, so at zero the prefix is suppressed and the reader is left with a dangling, ungrammatical fragment that reads like a rendering bug.
findings.fix: When the count is 0, render a complete sentence as the lead ('No open houses across Central Oregon this week') instead of the leading-space fragment; when it is 1+, keep the existing '<n> open houses across Central Oregon this week.' Never emit a lead that starts mid-phrase.

findings.title: No way to scope the open-house feed by date, city, or price
findings.evidence: The page offers no filter or date controls anywhere in the four panels. page.tsx:89-111 accepts `dateFrom/dateTo/community/city/minPrice/maxPrice/beds/baths` search params, but nothing on the page lets a user set them. The only interactive control is the hero's generic natural-language box ('3 bed under $800k in Bend with a shop', open-houses-desktop-01.png), which routes to /homes-for-sale (all listings), not to a filtered open-house feed. A visitor who wants 'open houses in Bend this Saturday' has no control to get there.
findings.fix: Add a lightweight filter/date bar above the feed (e.g. 'This weekend' / 'Upcoming' toggles plus city chips) that writes the search params the page already reads, so users can scope the open-house list without leaving the page.

findings.title: Hero's prominent actions are all generic/seller, none open-house-specific
findings.evidence: On this buyer-discovery page the hero's action cluster (open-houses-desktop-01.png) is a plain-language all-homes search plus 'BROWSE' and 'HOME WORTH?' buttons. page.tsx calls KbHero without passing `cta`/`ctaSecondary`, so it inherits the defaults (KbHero.client.tsx:94-97): Browse → /homes-for-sale and Home worth? → /sell/valuation. The single most prominent CTA set on an open-houses page points the user at all-homes browsing and a seller valuation form — nothing helps them find or plan an open house to attend.
findings.fix: Pass open-house-relevant hero CTAs — e.g. a primary that jumps to / anchors the feed ('See this weekend's open houses') and/or an 'Get open-house alerts' action — keeping 'Browse all homes' as the secondary rather than the default Browse/Home-worth pair.

findings.title: Full-height hero's CTAs send users away from the tool instead of into it
findings.evidence: tools-mortgage-desktop-01.png: the hero fills the entire viewport and its only two buttons are generic 'BROWSE →' and 'HOME WORTH?' which navigate off-page; the actual calculator sits one full screen below (tools-mortgage-desktop-02.png) with no downward cue. page.tsx (KbHero call, lines 101-110) passes no cta/ctaSecondary, so KbHero.client.tsx lines 94-97 fall back to the site-wide Browse / 'Home worth?' defaults. A user who came to calculate a payment is invited to leave before ever reaching the tool.
findings.fix: Override the hero CTAs for this page: primary 'Estimate my payment' anchoring to #calculator, secondary 'Browse homes'. Drop the terse, awkward 'Home worth?' label on this page.

findings.title: Calculator inputs show raw unformatted numbers while the result is currency-formatted
findings.evidence: tools-mortgage-desktop-02.png: the Home price field reads '500000', Property tax '6000', Home insurance '1750' with no thousands separators and no $ sign, sitting directly above a result that reads '$100,000 · Loan amount: $400,000' and '$3,174/month'. The single most important field forces the user to count digits, and the raw-vs-formatted mismatch on the same card looks unfinished. Source: MortgageCalculator.tsx lines 98-105 render type=number inputs bound to raw numeric state; only the result block calls formatCurrency.
findings.fix: Format the dollar inputs with thousands separators and a $ prefix (masked text input or format-on-blur) while keeping them editable, and apply font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums per the brand numeric rule.

findings.title: Flagship tool is a plain shadcn card double-framed inside the KB card, with a redundant title
findings.evidence: tools-mortgage-desktop-02.png: the calculator sits inside a navy hard-edge KB card that itself wraps a second bordered shadcn Card whose small plain-Geist 'Mortgage calculator' title just repeats the section heading 'YOUR MONTHLY PAYMENT' directly above it. The border-inside-a-border and default component styling make the page's core tool read as an unstyled drop-in against an otherwise polished editorial page. Source: page.tsx kb-tool-card border (line 123) + MortgageCalculator.tsx CardHeader/CardTitle (lines 90-93).
findings.fix: Remove the inner Card's border and the redundant CardTitle so there is a single frame; let the labels and inputs inherit the KB card surface.

findings.title: 'How to use' explainer is crammed into the left half while the right half is empty
findings.evidence: tools-mortgage-desktop-03.png: the three-paragraph explainer occupies only the left ~50% of the section and the entire right half is blank cream, so the guide looks unbalanced and unfinished at desktop width. Source: page.tsx ov-prose block, lines 145-162.
findings.fix: Widen the prose column or add a supporting element on the right (e.g. a short 'included / not included' list or the disclaimer as a callout) so the section fills the available width.

findings.title: Facebook sign-in label is muted gray while Google is full-strength, so the two parallel options look unequal
findings.evidence: In login-desktop-01.png the 'Continue with Facebook' label renders visibly lighter/grayer than 'Continue with Google' directly above it. Source confirms the mismatch: components/auth/LoginForm.tsx sets the Google button to `text-foreground` but the Facebook button to `text-muted-foreground`. Two equivalent auth paths at different text emphasis makes Facebook read as secondary or disabled and can suppress use of a valid login method.
findings.fix: Give both social buttons the same label color — change the Facebook button class from `text-muted-foreground` to `text-foreground` in LoginForm.tsx so the two options carry identical emphasis.

findings.title: Login card floats high with a large empty white band before the footer
findings.evidence: The card ends at 'Back to home' around mid-viewport in login-desktop-01.png, then a large white void follows; login-desktop-02.png / -03.png show the header, a blank band, then the footer. Source: app/login/page.tsx uses `min-h-[60vh]` with `justify-center`, which centers the card in the top 60% of the viewport and leaves the lower region empty above the rich footer, so the page reads unfinished on tall desktop screens.
findings.fix: Fill the viewport above the footer — raise the wrapper to roughly `min-h-[calc(100vh-<header>)]` (or center the card within the full available space) so the trailing whitespace band collapses.

findings.title: Header still shows a 'Sign in' CTA while the user is already on the sign-in page
findings.evidence: In login-desktop-01.png the top-right nav shows a 'Sign in' button even though this is /login; clicking it just reloads the same page. The destination equals the current page, a page-specific redundancy that adds a dead action to the primary conversion surface.
findings.fix: Suppress or set an inert active state on the header 'Sign in' link when the current route is /login (or /signup) so it is not offered as a navigation target on the page it points to.

findings.title: Facebook social button renders lower-contrast than the Google button
findings.evidence: In signup-desktop-01.png the two social buttons sit stacked and identical in size, but 'Continue with Facebook' text reads visibly grayer/weaker than 'Continue with Google'. Confirmed in components/auth/SignupForm.tsx: the Google button uses `text-foreground` while the Facebook button uses `text-muted-foreground`, so two equivalent auth options have unequal visual weight.
findings.fix: Change the Facebook button className from `text-muted-foreground` to `text-foreground` in SignupForm.tsx so both providers have identical label contrast.

findings.title: Password minimum of 6 characters signals a weak security floor
findings.evidence: signup-desktop-01.png shows the helper 'At least 6 characters' under the password field; SignupForm.tsx enforces `password.length < 6`. A 6-character minimum in 2026 reads as weak to security-aware users creating an account on a broker site holding their contact data.
findings.fix: Raise the minimum to at least 8 characters (update both the `password.length < 6` check and the 'At least 6 characters' hint) and consider a lightweight strength indicator.

findings.title: Full global mega-footer with a competing email-capture sits directly below the signup card
findings.evidence: signup-desktop-02.png shows the centered `max-w-md` signup card is followed by the full site footer, including the 'Bend real estate, monthly' newsletter block with its own email field + 'Subscribe' button and ~40 navigation links. On a dedicated conversion page this adds a second, competing email-capture CTA and many exit routes that pull focus from the single goal (create account).
findings.fix: On auth routes render a minimal footer (wordmark + legal links only) and suppress the newsletter block and mega-link columns to keep the page distraction-light.

findings.title: No spam/privacy reassurance next to the signup CTA
findings.evidence: signup-desktop-01.png: the card promises 'Save homes, get alerts, and stay in the loop' and collects name + email + password, but the only privacy signal is the fine-print Terms/Privacy links under the button. Notably the footer newsletter block explicitly reassures 'No spam' while the account form itself does not, so the higher-commitment action carries less reassurance than the lower one.
findings.fix: Add a one-line reassurance near the subtitle or the Create account button (e.g. 'We never share your email. Unsubscribe from alerts anytime.').
